skill.name: data-visualization-tool
skill.description: Create charts and visualizations in DBX Studio from SQL query results, including bar, line, pie, scatter, area, and histogram charts.
skill.summary: Build DBX Studio charts from SQL query results with clear chart type and axis guidance.
skill.author: Dbxstudio

content.value_statement: Turning raw query results into the right chart can take repeated setup. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code to choose chart types, write SELECT queries, and call DBX Studio chart generation.
actual_capabilities: Selects a chart type from bar, line, pie, scatter, area, and histogram options.
Maps common user intents, such as trends or breakdowns, to suitable chart choices.
Defines fields for DBX Studio chart generation, including title, axes, data query, and grouping.
Provides SELECT query patterns for categories, time series, and proportion breakdown charts.
Applies chart design rules for titles, readable axes, aggregation, and pie chart slice limits.
limitations: Does not include the implementation of the generate_chart tool.
Requires DBX Studio and database access that can run the selected SQL query.
Examples use generic order data and may need schema changes for real databases.
Does not validate permissions, query cost, or sensitive data exposure.

use_cases.title: Compare Category Performance
use_cases.description: Build a bar chart from grouped query results to compare products, regions, or segments.

use_cases.title: Track Trends Over Time
use_cases.description: Create line or area charts that summarize activity across days, weeks, or months.

use_cases.title: Prepare Clean Dashboard Inputs
use_cases.description: Aggregate query results before charting so dashboards stay readable and efficient.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Simple Chart
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a bar chart that compares total revenue by product category. Use clear axis labels and a short title.

prompt_templates.title: Choose the Best Chart Type
prompt_templates.prompt: I need to show customer growth over the last 12 months. Choose the best chart type and explain the title and axes.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Query Driven Chart
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a line chart for daily order volume during the last 30 days. Use aggregated results and readable date labels.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Multi Metric View
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan charts for revenue, order count, and status share in one dashboard. Select chart types, queries, labels, and aggregation levels.

output_examples.output: The assistant recommends a bar chart with category labels on the x-axis, revenue on the y-axis, and a grouped revenue query.

output_examples.input: Show order volume for the last 30 days.
output_examples.output: The assistant recommends a line chart using daily totals, a title that includes the date range, and readable date labels.

output_examples.input: Show the share of orders by status.
output_examples.output: The assistant recommends a pie chart when there are seven or fewer statuses and groups extra statuses as Other.

best_practices: Aggregate data before charting to reduce noise and improve performance.
Use chart titles that include the metric and time period when relevant.
Limit pie charts to seven slices and group smaller categories as Other.
anti_patterns: Do not chart raw row-level data when an aggregate view answers the question.
Do not use pie charts for many categories or precise comparisons.
Do not keep raw column names when human-readable axis labels are available.

faq.question: What chart types does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers bar, line, pie, scatter, area, and histogram charts.

faq.question: Does it write SQL?
faq.answer: It provides SELECT query patterns and asks the assistant to adapt them to the database schema.

faq.question: Can it build DBX Studio dashboards?
faq.answer: It can plan chart inputs for dashboards, but dashboard layout depends on DBX Studio features outside this skill.

faq.question: Does it execute database queries?
faq.answer: No. It guides the assistant to prepare queries and chart configuration for the available DBX Studio tools.

faq.question: How does it choose chart types?
faq.answer: It maps user intent, such as comparison or trend, to the chart type that best matches the data.

faq.question: What should users provide?
faq.answer: Users should provide the metric, time range, grouping fields, and any database schema details they know.
